checks.command: live MCP policy lifecycle against rebuilt Compose web and persistent D1
checks.summary: Observed 44 of 44 tools default-denied; unauthenticated mutation returned 401; agent scope expansion returned 409; workspace allow plus agent deny resolved to deny; stale revision returned 409; revoke took status to revoked; re-register and reconnect restored connected.

Restored the exercised workspace and agent decisions to inherit, recreated the web container without the temporary in-memory administrator token, verified MCP_ADMIN_TOKEN is not configured, and left the MCP server connected.

securityEvidence: Policy evaluation is deny unless the workspace explicitly allows the exact server and tool; agent policy can inherit or deny but cannot broaden the workspace ceiling.
Risk and approval fields are derived from the server-side discovered descriptor and are not accepted from policy mutation bodies.
Only explicitly allowed read tools are materialized for model use. Write, execute, external, or approval-labelled tools remain unavailable until a resumable payload-bound approval bridge exists.
Every MCP transport invocation re-checks workspace and agent decision, policy revision, server revision and status, current allowlist membership, current endpoint, and current credential fingerprint.
Regression tests prove revoked/disconnected servers, stale revisions, new agent denies, removed allowlist entries, missing secrets, and credential rotation all cause zero transport calls.
Policy mutation requires the server-side administrator credential, optimistic revision, and idempotency key; actor identity cannot be supplied by the request body.
Policy audit is append-only. Stored and returned audit records contain no tool arguments, authorization headers, bearer values, API key fields, token fields, or secret references.
The portal holds its administrator token only in React component memory and uses a password field with storage disabled.
knownLimits: Side-effecting MCP tools intentionally remain unavailable; P3-T2 does not weaken payload-bound approval requirements to make them appear usable.
The administrator token is deliberately unconfigured after live smoke cleanup. An operator must supply MCP_ADMIN_TOKEN at runtime before making policy changes through the portal.
The Docker MCP Gateway image is still the floating latest tag and is deferred to P6-T1 image pinning and vulnerability evidence.

Live revoke/reconnect was validated through the real registry and D1 API; zero transport after revocation is deterministically proven by invocation-wrapper tests rather than relying on nondeterministic model tool choice.
publication: No orchestrator submission/review, commit, push, merge, deployment, publication, or real secret change was performed by this worker.
